evidence: commit dff549e -- Task 4 (F2 app-half closed: auth gate enforced by default)
commit 7a008ad -- Task 5 (F2 infra-half closed: mcp-auth-token resolved from Key Vault)
assertion.rationale: F1: data-api's external boundary (ingressExternal: true) had no inbound authentication, so the estate's external communications boundary was neither monitored nor controlled for anyone who discovered the FQDN. F1 is now CLOSED (Task 6): infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep's dataApiApp module sets ingressExternal:false, so data-api is no longer an external boundary at all — it is reachable only from inside the Container Apps environment, through the nginx proxy both frontends already ran. F2: mcp-tools' external boundary is required to stay open (Copilot Studio calls it from the internet); the auth gate meant to protect that boundary was inert in the shipped configuration, so the control the repo advertises most prominently at its key internal/external boundary was not actually enforced. F2 is now CLOSED (Tasks 4 and 5). Task 4 closed the application half: enforcement no longer keys off backendMode, so the gate now fails closed at this boundary by default in every mode, and is mounted ahead of the body parser so an unauthenticated caller cannot make the process do work before the boundary check runs. Task 5 closed the infra half: MLS_TOOL_BACKENDS is now set explicitly (mcpToolsBackendMode, default 'local') rather than being absent, and the token the boundary check compares against is resolved from the platform Key Vault at runtime via the mcp-tools UAMI's Key Vault Secrets User grant (keyVaultUrl reference, infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep module mcpKvGrant) rather than depending on an operator remembering to wire a secure parameter through infra/ or CI that nothing ever did. Overall status is now CLOSED: both findings this control cites are closed — the estate's remaining external boundary (mcp-tools) is authenticated by design, and data-api no longer has an external boundary to authenticate. This control has no other open contributors (checked: no other finding in compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md cites 3.13.1). CORRECTION (2026-08-28, final pre-publication audit -- F25). The sentence above about Task 6 closing F1 was written from F1's own Fix text and was INCOMPLETE, and the clause it leaned on -- "both frontends already proxy /api/ server-side" -- was the bypass rather than the reason internal ingress sufficed. control-tower and launch-ops were themselves ingressExternal:true with NO authConfig, and both nginx.conf.template files blind-proxy `location /api/ { proxy_pass ${DATA_API_ORIGIN}/; }` with no credential and no path allowlist, so GET https://<control-tower-fqdn>/api/feeds/secure-score reached data-api unauthenticated from the public internet -- against an identity holding Security Reader at SUBSCRIPTION scope. F25 closes it: infra/bicep/apps/main.bicep now puts Container Apps Easy Auth (entraEasyAuthConfig(), RedirectToLoginPage, an Entra provider with only a public clientId and openIdIssuer, tokenStore disabled, no client secret) in front of launch-ops, control-tower AND compliance, and each app's ingressExternal is the same expression as "is Easy Auth configured", so no parameter combination publishes one of them without authentication. excludedPaths is ['/healthz'] and nothing else, so nothing under /api/ is reachable without a session. .github/workflows/layer-07-apps.yml resolves MLS_LAUNCH_OPS_CLIENT_ID, MLS_CONTROL_TOWER_CLIENT_ID and MLS_COMPLIANCE_CLIENT_ID from the Entra app registrations L3 creates, treating a hand-set variable as an override; an ID it cannot resolve leaves that app internal-only rather than failing the deploy or publishing it open (F36 -- an earlier revision of this workflow refused to deploy at all without all three, which made the F25 fix undeployable out of the box, and is the claim this sentence used to carry). F26, found alongside it: the runbook's claim that an unset MLS_COMPLIANCE_CLIENT_ID made ARM reject the deployment was false -- an undefined GitHub variable expands to the EMPTY STRING, so readEnvironmentVariable returned '' and never reached its 'unset' default (reproduced against Bicep CLI 0.46.1); the guard now treats empty and 'unset' alike. Verified by verification/tests/frontend-auth.Tests.ps1 (14 assertions, each mutation-tested) and az bicep build; nothing has been deployed. The overall status stays CLOSED, but on a different and now-checked basis: the estate's external boundaries are mcp-tools (token-authenticated) and the three human-facing apps (Entra-authenticated at the ingress). data-api is not an external boundary and, since F25, is no longer reachable THROUGH one either.

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. (Setting ingressExternal:false on data-api, Task 6, and the MCP auth gate default and Key Vault token resolution for mcp-tools' boundary, Tasks 4 and 5, are all DONE.) A regression here — external ingress re-added to data-api, or the mcp-tools auth gate re-keyed to a mode that isn't shipped — would reopen this control.
